item.description: An earthquake of magnitude five struck Tibet on Thursday. Rescue operations continue following catastrophic flooding near the Gyirong border crossing. Landslides continue to pose a significant concern for rescue teams. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: El Niño de 2026 podría ser el más fuerte jamás registrado, según la autoridad meteorológica de EE. UU.
item.description: El Niño de 2026 se perfila como un episodio de intensidad excepcional y podría convertirse en el más fuerte jamás registrado. Además, podría prolongarse hasta febrero de 2027 y ya coincide con fuertes anomalías en la temperatura del océano, alteraciones de las lluvias y afectaciones a la agricultura en varias regiones. En el Pacífico, una inusual sucesión de dos huracanes y una tormenta tropical refleja las condiciones extremas asociadas al fenómeno. Fuente: France 24 - Español.

item.title: A Wyoming ranch was bought for conservation, but cattle stayed to protect it
item.description: A Wyoming ranch proved cattle grazing can protect ecosystems. Conservationists bought Red Canyon Ranch and kept cattle grazing to test coexistence. Managed grazing mimics historical patterns, supporting grasslands and diverse plant communities. This approach informs conservation strategies across the American West today. The ranch serves as a model for balancing agriculture and biodiversity goals. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: ‘Supersizing before our eyes’: UN warns of record El Niño approaching
item.description: Event is likely to be largest in at least 1,000 years and will pile extra heat into a world already in a climate crisis The El Niño climate phenomenon is “supersizing before our eyes”, the UN has said. The event is near certain to shatter temperature records, according to the latest forecasts. The El Niño is likely to be the largest in at least 1,000 years and will pile extra heat into an atmosphere where temperatures are already rising rapidly due to global heating. The combination means 2027 is set to “ blow apart ” the record and be the hottest year ever recorded . Continue reading... Fuente: The Guardian - Environment.

item.title: The September reset is real. I’m about to become a better person, flaxseed by flaxseed | Emma Brockes
item.description: Small changes are what I’m aiming for – 10-minute workouts, cleaning out my handbag. Then I’m less likely to have failed come October Are you a January resolutions or a September reset person? The latter has always felt more propitious to me, light of the exhaustion of Christmas and with the weather still on our side. Last week, when the Pavlovian response to buying new stationery (for my kids) kicked in, I found myself following a rote impulse to sort my life out by replacing the bag in the vacuum cleaner and committing to an unsustainable course of personal change. item.title: Desde el terreno: Haití, entre el hambre, la violencia y la amenaza de la sequía
item.description: Haití atraviesa una de las peores crisis humanitarias de su historia reciente: 5,8 millones de personas enfrentan inseguridad alimentaria aguda y más de 1,4 millones han sido desplazadas por la violencia. En el noroeste del país, muchas familias buscan sobrevivir cultivando la tierra y criando animales, pero la pobreza, la falta de recursos y la amenaza de nuevas sequías ponen en riesgo sus cosechas. item.title: The future of Alaskan wildfire detailed in new climate model study
item.description: Climate change is altering patterns of wildfire activity in Alaska, making fires larger and more common in some areas with historically low fire activity. Wildfires can be difficult to predict because they are affected by intricate interactions among factors including climate, ecology and weather. But a better idea of which fire pathways are more likely is important for future fire forecasting, adaptation and management strategies. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: California could unlock $100M-$200M in annual water value by using better forecasts at 20 reservoirs
item.description: To boost water availability in California, advanced weather forecast models can play a crucial role. item.title: Scientists released 45,000 cfs from Glen Canyon Dam for 8 days in 1996 to rebuild Grand Canyon sandbars
item.description: In 1996, a controlled flood was executed in the Grand Canyon to rejuvenate its natural river dynamics.
